introduction: At this level, we memorize the important 'Parallel' lines of the world and the historical borders associated with World War I, World War II, and the Cold War.

core_concepts.title: 49th Parallel
core_concepts.description:
Countries: **USA & Canada**. 
Key Feature: It forms the longest and most peaceful international border in the world.

core_concepts.title: 38th Parallel
core_concepts.description:
Countries: **North Korea & South Korea**. 
Key Feature: It serves as a Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) dividing the Korean Peninsula into two hostile nations.

core_concepts.title: Maginot Line
core_concepts.description:
Countries: **France & Germany**. 
History: A massive line of concrete fortifications and weapons installations built by France after WWI to deter invasion by Germany.

core_concepts.title: Hindenburg Line
core_concepts.description:
Countries: **Germany & Poland**. 
History: It was a formidable German defensive line built during World War I.

core_concepts.title: LoC vs. LAC
core_concepts.description:
1. **LoC (Line of Control):** The military control line between India and Pakistan in Kashmir (established after the 1972 Shimla Agreement). 
2. **LAC (Line of Actual Control):** The demarcation line that separates Indian-controlled territory from Chinese-controlled territory (established post the 1962 war).

important_entities.name: 17th Parallel
important_entities.significance: Before the Vietnam War ended, this line separated communist North Vietnam from South Vietnam. (Today, Vietnam is a single unified country).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
The Biggest Exam Confusion: 
- 38th Parallel = Korea (Highly tense and militarized border). 
- 49th Parallel = USA-Canada (Highly peaceful border).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: France built a 'Magic Knot' (Maginot) to keep the Germans out.

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite State PCS/UPSC question: 'The 38th Parallel divides which two countries?' Answer: North Korea and South Korea.
